prompt.context_jp: 向こうから歩いてきたスーツ姿の男___、こちらに気づくことなく角を曲がっていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 向こうから歩いてきたスーツ姿の男___、こちらに気づくことなく角を曲がっていく。

feedback.correct_en: This sentence introduces the suited man for the first time — he's new information appearing on the scene. New-information subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest the man is already an established topic, but he's being introduced here as someone walking toward them.

contrast_examples.en: A man came walking (newly on scene).

contrast_examples.jp: その男は去っていった。

prompt.context_jp: 頬が火照っているのか、血の気___引いているのか、自分でもよく分からない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頬が火照っているのか、血の気___引いているのか、自分でもよく分からない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the second alternative.

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is a fixed expression ('blood draining'); 血の気 is the subject of the intransitive 引く, so が is used.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 血の気 a direct object, but 引く here is intransitive ('to recede') — the blood itself recedes.

contrast_examples.en: The color drains from one's face.

prompt.context_jp: 「いや 隠れますよ 普通 ___もの！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いや 隠れますよ 普通 ___もの！」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in what Mai says about running into her ex.

feedback.correct_en: 気まずい ('awkward') captures the uncomfortable feeling of running into an ex — exactly what justifies hiding.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気持ちいい ('pleasant') and うれしい ('happy') are the opposite feeling and wouldn't explain why she hid.

contrast_examples.jp: 元彼に会うのは気まずい。
旧友に会えてうれしい。
contrast_examples.en: I'm happy to see an old friend.

prompt.context_jp: 「ああ 今 連絡___あって 取引先から預かった約束手形を 紛失してしまったらしいんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ああ 今 連絡___あって 取引先から預かった約束手形を 紛失してしまったらしいんだよ」

feedback.correct_en: The deputy manager is reporting new information — a call just came in. 連絡 is being introduced as a new event, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 連絡 as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit announcing fresh news.

contrast_examples.en: A phone call came in (new event).

contrast_examples.jp: その電話は昨日の件です。
contrast_examples.en: That call is about yesterday's matter (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: もしホントに 紛失してたんだとしたら大ごとだぞ 支店のみならず 銀行全体の信用___関わるんだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 支店のみならず 銀行全体の信用___関わるんだ

feedback.correct_en: 〜に関わる ('to concern/affect') takes に to mark what is affected. Here, it affects the bank's credibility.
feedback.incorrect_en: を関わる is ungrammatical; 関わる is intransitive and pairs with に.

contrast_examples.en: It's a matter of life and death.

prompt.context_jp: たった一枚の紙切れ___、これほど大勢の人間を動かしているのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: たった一枚の紙切れ___、これほど大勢の人間を動かしているのだ。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is marveling that it's precisely this one slip of paper (exhaustive/emphatic) causing so much commotion — が emphasizes 'this specific thing is what's doing it.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a neutral topic statement, losing the emphatic 'of all things, just this one piece of paper' nuance that fits the dramatic framing.

contrast_examples.jp: たった一人が全てを変えた。

prompt.context_jp: 臨店班___支店で歓迎されることは、まずない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 臨店班___支店で歓迎されることは、まずない。

feedback.correct_en: Inside the nominalized clause (〜が支店で歓迎される), 臨店班 is the subject of the passive verb 歓迎される, so が marks it.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make 臨店班 a direct object, but with the passive 歓迎される, the thing being welcomed is the subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「本部から___ 臨店班の相馬です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「本部から___ 臨店班の相馬です」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the humble verb form Souma uses when introducing himself.

feedback.correct_en: まいる is the humble (kenjōgo) form of 来る/行く, appropriate when humbly describing one's own action to a client or senior.
feedback.incorrect_en: いらっしゃる is honorific (sonkeigo) — used for the listener's actions, not your own. 行きました is plain polite and lacks the business formality.

contrast_examples.jp: 本部からまいりました。
社長がいらっしゃいました。

prompt.context_jp: 相馬___気にも留めない様子で、フロアを見渡しながら行員たちの動きを目で追っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬___気にも留めない様子で、フロアを見渡しながら行員たちの動きを目で追っていた。

feedback.correct_en: Souma is the established topic of the scene. The sentence describes what he (as topic) is doing, contrasting implicitly with Mai's reaction, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly introduce Souma as if he weren't already in the scene, but he's been there throughout.

prompt.context_jp: 「この男なんですよ 手形を___のは なあ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この男なんですよ 手形を___のは なあ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in what Noguchi says about Horita losing the note.

feedback.correct_en: 〜てくれた here is sarcastic — Noguchi literally says 'the one who kindly lost it for me,' using the favor-receiving form ironically to express blame.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜てあげた ('did [the losing] for someone else') doesn't fit the speaker's own grievance. 〜てもらった would require a different grammatical frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 面倒を起こしてくれたな。
手伝ってくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: 児玉の口元___は、隠しきれない笑みが浮かんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 児玉の口元___は、隠しきれない笑みが浮かんでいた。

feedback.correct_en: に marks the location where a state exists — the smile exists on his lips. 浮かぶ (to appear/float) describes a static appearance at a location, pairing with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action, but here no action is being performed — a smile is simply present on his face.

contrast_examples.en: A smile appears on the face.

prompt.context_jp: ところが、真藤の表情___ぴくりとも動かない。
prompt.prompt_jp: ところが、真藤の表情___ぴくりとも動かない。

feedback.correct_en: ところが signals a contrast with the previous sentence (Kodama expected delight). は marks Shindō's expression contrastively — 'his expression, by contrast, didn't move.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply assert a new fact, missing the contrastive 'but, however' flavor set up by ところが.

contrast_examples.jp: ところが彼は笑わなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「手形の紛失___ 東京第一銀行の 信用に関わる不祥事だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「手形の紛失___ 東京第一銀行の 信用に関わる不祥事だ」

feedback.correct_en: Shindō is defining/characterizing what the lost note means — 'As for the loss of the note, it is a scandal.' This is a classic topic-comment definitional sentence requiring は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as newly identifying which thing is the scandal, but Shindō is making a sweeping declaration about an already-known event.

prompt.context_jp: 受け取りから帰店まで、手形___堀田の手元にあったはずの時間は決して短くない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 受け取りから帰店まで、手形___堀田の手元にあったはずの時間は決して短くない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the embedded clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 時間 ('the time during which the note was in Horita's hands'), the subject takes が, not は. Relative-clause subjects almost always use が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally cannot appear inside a relative clause as the subject of the modifying verb — it would break the clause structure.

contrast_examples.en: He wrote a book (main clause topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「じゃ やっぱり 手形___ 支店の中にあるということですよね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「じゃ やっぱり 手形___ 支店の中にあるということですよね」

feedback.correct_en: The note is the established topic of the whole investigation. Souma is drawing a conclusion about it: 'as for the note, it must be in the branch.' は fits topic-based reasoning.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly identify which item is in the branch, but the note has been the topic all along.

contrast_examples.en: The note is in the branch (about it).

prompt.context_jp: 必要なのは、一つひとつの事実を丁寧に___ことだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 必要なのは、一つひとつの事実を丁寧に___ことだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'to build up facts one by one.'

feedback.correct_en: 積み上げる ('to stack up/accumulate') is the standard collocation with 事実 — gradually building up evidence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 積み下ろす means 'unload' and 積み込む means 'load (onto)' — neither matches the metaphor of accumulating facts.

prompt.context_jp: 野口の怒声が響いたあと、フロア___は重苦しい沈黙が落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 野口の怒声が響いたあと、フロア___は重苦しい沈黙が落ちた。

feedback.correct_en: 落ちる here describes silence settling onto/into the floor — a state coming into existence at a location. に marks the destination/location of appearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks where an action occurs; here silence is not performing an action but descending upon the location.

prompt.context_jp: 人が何かを捜すとき、目___どうしても「ありそうな所」にばかり向きがちだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 人が何かを捜すとき、目___どうしても「ありそうな所」にばかり向きがちだ。

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic statement about how 'the eye' behaves — a general truth with 目 as the topic. は marks generic topics in universal statements.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would describe a specific instance of eyes turning, but this sentence is a general observation about human behavior.

prompt.context_jp: 「私 今 本部の臨店班にいるんです 今日___ 手形の件で来ました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今日___ 手形の件で来ました」

feedback.correct_en: Mai is setting 'today' as the topic/frame — 'as for today, I came regarding the note.' Time expressions used as the frame of a statement typically take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 今日が would exhaustively identify 'today' (as opposed to other days) as when she came, which doesn't fit the casual explanation.

prompt.context_jp: 「会いたくない人に バッタリ会って ___なぁって思ってたら 香澄さんに会えるなんて やっぱり 私 ツイてます！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ツイてない___なぁって思ってたら…やっぱり 私 ツイてます！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what Mai says about her luck.

feedback.correct_en: ツイてない means 'unlucky' — the opposite of ツイてる ('lucky'), which Mai says at the end. The contrast makes ツイてない the right fit.
feedback.incorrect_en: つまらない ('boring') and もったいない ('wasteful') don't form the lucky/unlucky contrast with ツイてる.

prompt.context_jp: 行員たちは誰も顔を上げず、フロア___水を打ったように静まり返っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロア___水を打ったように静まり返っている。

feedback.correct_en: The floor is already the established scene. The narrator is describing its state ('as for the floor, it was dead silent'), so は marks the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly introduce the floor as if it hadn't been in view, but the floor is the ongoing setting.

prompt.context_jp: 誰一人として、堀田___かばおうとする者はいなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰一人として、堀田___かばおうとする者はいなかった。

feedback.correct_en: かばう ('to protect/cover for') is a transitive verb; Horita is the one being protected (direct object), so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make Horita the subject of かばう, meaning 'Horita tries to protect [someone],' which reverses the meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 部下がかばってくれた。

prompt.context_jp: 堀田さんの責任を___前に どうやったら見つかるのか 考えるほうが先決だと思います！
prompt.prompt_jp: 堀田さんの責任を___前に…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'before holding Horita responsible'.

feedback.correct_en: 責任を問う is the set phrase for 'to hold [someone] accountable / to call into question their responsibility.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 聞く and 尋ねる both mean 'to ask' in the sense of inquiring, but they don't form the fixed phrase 責任を〜 meaning 'to hold accountable.'

prompt.context_jp: Kasumi casually tells Mai about her recent breakup.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for Kasumi in this casual conversation among friends at a bar?

choices.text: つきあってた人がいたんだけど、最近 別れちゃった。
交際しておりました者がおりましたが、先日 別離いたしました。

feedback.correct_en: The casual conversational register with 〜ちゃった and んだけど fits the friendly bar setting between former colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second option uses stiff humble/formal vocabulary (おります, 交際, 別離) that would sound absurd in a casual chat with a close kōhai.

contrast_examples.en: We broke up (casual, with a tinge of regret).

prompt.context_jp: Souma addresses the angry client Kawabata.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Souma apologizing to the client as a bank representative?

choices.text: 私どもといたしましても、今回の事態は大変 重く受け止めております。
俺たちも、今回のことはマジで重く見てるよ。

feedback.correct_en: When formally apologizing to an angry client, bank officials use 私ども, いたしましても, and 受け止めております — polished humble language.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺たち and マジで are casual-rough speech completely inappropriate for a corporate apology to a client.

contrast_examples.jp: 重く受け止めております。

prompt.context_jp: 「君が帰るとき ちょうど___に来たよな？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「君が帰るとき ちょうど___に来たよな？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression for 'they arrived just as you were leaving (crossing paths).'

feedback.correct_en: 入れ違い describes two people passing each other at a doorway — one leaving as the other enters. Perfect for the described timing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 間違い means 'mistake'; 行き違い typically means miscommunication or missing each other en route, not a face-to-face passing at a doorway.

contrast_examples.en: They came just as the other left.

prompt.context_jp: Mai excitedly proposes retracing Horita's steps.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for Mai's energetic suggestion to her partner Souma?

choices.text: 相馬さん、今から そのファミレス 行きましょう！
相馬様におかれましては、当該ファミリーレストランへご同行賜りたく存じます。

feedback.correct_en: Mai talks to her senior partner in standard polite 行きましょう form — energetic, direct, and appropriate for colleagues on fieldwork.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second option is bureaucratic over-honorific language (〜におかれましては, 賜りたく) that no one would use with a coworker.

contrast_examples.jp: ご同行賜りたく存じます。
contrast_examples.en: I humbly request your accompaniment (absurd for coworkers).

prompt.context_jp: Souma teasing Mai after she hid from her ex.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Souma's casual tease?

choices.text: お前が 街角で元彼にバッタリ出会ったら 隠れるタイプとはねえ
あなたが 街角にて元彼氏と偶然遭遇した際 隠匿する類型とは意外です

feedback.correct_en: Casual spoken Japanese uses お前, バッタリ, 元彼, and the sentence-final とはねえ — natural teasing register between coworker-friends.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second version swaps every word for a stiff Sino-Japanese formal equivalent (遭遇, 隠匿, 類型) — unidiomatic for casual banter.

prompt.context_jp: Noguchi is yelling at Horita in front of the whole branch.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Noguchi's furious, blunt yelling at Horita?

choices.text: お前のせいで 三鷹支店 大迷惑だよ！
あなたのおかげさまで、三鷹支店は少々お困りの状態です。

feedback.correct_en: お前のせいで and the barking tone fit a branch manager publicly dressing down a subordinate in anger.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたのおかげさまで (politely 'thanks to you') and the softened phrasing are totally wrong for a shouted reprimand.
